title: A Letter for the Compass
premise: In 1794, as the Republic of Valcourt collapses under advancing imperial armies, Marguerite Vasquez serves as a courier carrying coded letters for a government that has already forgotten them. When imperial forces requisition the border town of Saint-Aubin and seize the registry ledger containing the names of every family marked for deportation, Marguerite learns their own name is in it—and so are the names of the innkeeper's family who sheltered them. Over eleven desperate days, they must smuggle the ledger's evidence past three military checkpoints to reach a neutral envoy, discovering along the way that survival bought through invisibility has cost them every real connection they might have had. In the end, Marguerite delivers the ledger but chooses to stay behind with the found family they once kept at arm's length, trading their safe passage for a shared, uncertain future.
about_author: Juniper Pemberton is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing displaced persons' records from eighteenth-century border conflicts. They write historical fiction about the people history files under 'miscellaneous.'

chapters.title: The Weight of Blank Paper
chapters.summary: Marguerite arrives in Saint-Aubin carrying diplomatic cipher letters, posing as a clerk. POV: Marguerite. They observe the town's rhythms from the edges, cataloguing exits and habits. The emotional beat is practiced detachment—Marguerite has learned to love places the way one loves train platforms: briefly, without unpacking.

chapters.title: The Innkeeper's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Odile Ferrand, the widowed innkeeper, sees through Marguerite's clerk disguise in a single evening but says nothing, instead feeding them stew and assigning them a room. POV: Marguerite. Beat: warmth offered without conditions, which Marguerite doesn't know how to accept. Her daughter Sylvie asks too many questions.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Silences
chapters.summary: A flashback chapter: Marguerite's recruitment and first mission, when a misdelivered letter got a family arrested and taught them that silence is survival. POV: Marguerite. The beat is grief transmuted into discipline—we learn why they never stay, never speak, never keep anything.

chapters.title: Drums on the North Road
chapters.summary: Imperial outriders appear on the horizon; the Republic's garrison begins evacuating, and the town's officials burn what papers they can. POV: Marguerite. Beat: dread. Marguerite's handler orders them to wait for final instructions, trapping them in a town about to fall.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Holds
chapters.summary: The requisition begins. Imperial officers seize the town registry—the ledger listing every resident, including deportation classifications. POV: Marguerite. Beat: cold recognition. Marguerite glimpses the ledger and understands its power: names, allegiances, and the Ferrands marked 'removable.'

chapters.title: Invisible Was a Story I Told Myself
chapters.summary: Marguerite discovers their own alias in the ledger's courier index—the Republic sold its couriers' covers in the surrender terms. POV: Marguerite. Beat: betrayal and vertigo. The identity they built to survive is now the thing that will kill them.

chapters.title: Three Checkpoints, One Road
chapters.summary: Marguerite maps the route south: the bridge checkpoint, the abbey checkpoint, and the customs house at the frontier, each more dangerous than the last. POV: Marguerite. Beat: grim resolve. They begin planning to steal the ledger alone, telling no one—old habit as armor.

chapters.title: Sylvie Counts the Candles
chapters.summary: Sylvie Ferrand catches Marguerite copying cipher keys by candlelight and, instead of turning them in, offers to help—she can pass through the abbey checkpoint as a novice delivering alms. POV: Sylvie. Beat: defiant hope meeting Marguerite's terror of involving anyone.

chapters.title: The Cost of Being Known
chapters.summary: Marguerite refuses Sylvie's help and Odile intervenes, forcing the first honest conversation of Marguerite's adult life: invisibility kept you alive, she says, but it never kept you living. POV: Marguerite. Beat: painful self-recognition; the found family theme surfaces.

chapters.title: A Plan Made of Ordinary People
chapters.summary: The household assembles an unlikely crew: Odile's cart, Sylvie's novice cover, the blacksmith Tomas with his requisition passes, and old Père Anselme who knows the abbey's hidden stair. POV: Marguerite. Beat: cautious belonging—Marguerite plans a group operation for the first time and hates how much it steadies them.

chapters.title: The Night of Stolen Ink
chapters.summary: Marguerite breaks into the requisitioned records office to steal the ledger, finding it already moved—and a Republic officer, half-dead, who reveals the envoy at the frontier will only act on the ledger plus a countersignature Marguerite must forge. POV: Marguerite. Beat: stakes escalate; the mission is now forgery as well as theft.

chapters.title: Checkpoint One: The Bridge
chapters.summary: The cart crosses the river bridge under Tomas's passes while an imperial lieutenant interrogates Odile about her husband's old debts. POV: Sylvie. Beat: white-knuckle suspense; Sylvie watches Marguerite lie beautifully and realizes they've done this alone their whole life.

chapters.title: The Abbey's Long Shadow
chapters.summary: At the abbey, Père Anselme hides the group, but a wounded deserter in the crypt recognizes Marguerite's cipher training and begs to be smuggled too. POV: Marguerite. Beat: moral weight—taking him risks everything; leaving him makes them the Republic they no longer believe in.

chapters.title: What We Owe the Dead
chapters.summary: The deserter, Luc, reveals the deportation trains leave in four days—the timeline collapses. Marguerite takes him in. POV: Luc, briefly, then Marguerite. Beat: the price of survival made literal; every extra body on the cart is a debt Marguerite chooses to owe.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Two: The Abbey Gate
chapters.summary: The group exits through the abbey's hidden stair into a supply column, Sylvie walking among real novices, the ledger sewn into Odile's mattress. POV: Sylvie. Beat: terror and exhilaration; a near-discovery when a sergeant demands the mattress be unloaded, resolved by Odile's flawless nerve.

chapters.title: The Turncoat's Road
chapters.summary: A Republic defector turned imperial informant patrols the south road—Marguerite recognizes him as the handler who sold the couriers' covers. POV: Marguerite. Beat: fury versus caution; personal vengeance and the mission collide on the same muddy road.

chapters.title: Broken Cipher
chapters.summary: Imperial cryptographers intercept a Republic message and begin systematically checking travelers' papers against courier profiles—Marguerite's forged identity will not survive the customs house. POV: Marguerite. Beat: despair. The plan is dead; someone else must carry the ledger through.

chapters.title: The Hand That Signs
chapters.summary: Odile volunteers to carry the ledger through the customs house as a widow shipping her husband's effects; Marguerite must forge the countersignature and teach her the courier hand in one night. POV: Odile. Beat: role reversal—the protected becomes the protector; Marguerite learns what it costs to be loved enough to be risked for.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Three: The Customs House
chapters.summary: Odile walks the ledger through while Marguerite creates a diversion at the gate—deliberately being caught as a courier to burn their own cover and draw the defector's eye. POV: Marguerite. Beat: the climax's first half—Marguerite surrenders the invisible self that kept them alive, and is arrested.

chapters.title: Names in the Fire
chapters.summary: Interrogated, Marguerite gives the imperial captain a false ledger index, buying Odile time to reach the envoy; Luc and Tomas stage the escape Marguerite never asked for. POV: Marguerite. Beat: climax—the price of survival is finally paid in full, and it is paid by other people, which breaks Marguerite's oldest rule.

chapters.title: The Envoy's Decision
chapters.summary: The ledger and forged countersignature reach the neutral envoy; the deportations are halted by diplomatic intervention, and the defector is exposed. POV: Sylvie. Beat: relief shadowed by cost—the town is saved, but Marguerite lies wounded and their Republic is gone for good.

chapters.title: A Letter for the Compass
chapters.summary: Recovering at the inn, Marguerite writes their final report, then burns it, and instead writes a letter with no cipher at all—addressed to no handler, just to the household. POV: Marguerite. Beat: resolution—Marguerite chooses a name on a page, a family at a table, and a future with no exit route, and finds they no longer need one.
